limits: Representative selectors/states, not an exhaustive WCAG certification or screen-reader audit.
Only Chromium measured; separate browser matrices cover layout/axe in WebKit.
Opaque and translucent backgrounds are raster sampled; text foreground uses computed RGBA instead of anti-aliased glyph edge pixels.
CSS ancestor opacity or non-normal blend modes would be skipped rather than inferred.
Very small/subpixel probability bars and raster social-preview text are not certified by these measurements.
Low-ratio decorative team-color chips are permitted only with adjacent written team identity; their colors are not treated as a text contrast pass.
Eight compound table-header selectors had no direct text node and were skipped; other measured column labels do not certify those skipped nodes.
The deployed representative league pages did not expose every source-warning state; the archived Share warning was measured.
The sampled landing feature is opaque in the final design; the sticky header is the translucent plane. This does not certify every ambient-field position.
EPL/cricket had no visible zone-none bars for this selector; the shared neutral rule was measured with the NBA lower-seed distribution in four viewport/theme cases.
methodCorrections: Two 375px EPL header text ranges initially extended past their ellipsized container into a sibling SVG. Rechecked with overflow-ancestor clipping; the corrected light/dark ratios are 16.293/15.375. No product styling changed.

manualAriaReview.finding: aria-label is not well supported on this generic div. The visible “2026 champions” context and Royal Challengers Bengaluru name already communicate the information.
manualAriaReview.leadRepair: The lead removed the redundant aria-label locally after this 4089f17 production capture. Fresh 303 Python tests (one skip), 120 Vitest tests, lint and both builds pass. All 24 affected cricket browser cases pass across both bases, Chromium/WebKit, 320/375/1280px and both themes; aria-prohibited-attr incomplete is absent in all 24. Production smoke after deployment remains owned by the lead.
